node.title: Re: Perl Script to Run other Scripts with proper pauses?
node.author: Eily
node.doctext:
As usual with perl, there is more than one way to do it. You might just use [doc://system] to call a new perl process, but the more standard way to do it would be to use [doc://do]. You can set @ARGV to define the parameters for the other scrips. { local @ARGV = ("Two", "Parameters"); do "other_script.pl"; } #here other_script's execution is done If other_script returns a true value (eg: the last line in other_script.pl is "1") then you can write: { local @ARGV = (); do "other_script.pl" or die "Other script failed: $@"; } Error information will likely be in $@, but you might need to check $!, read [doc://do]'s documentation for more detail.

Edit: the advantages of [doc://do] over [doc://system] are that it does not create a separate perl process, and the output is usable as perl data.
